reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the correct handling: the cited paragraphs (§6 documentation rights, §3(e) usage-statistics access, §8(f) anti-spamming technical mechanisms) contain no audit, inspection or records-examination right running against Client, and none of them creates frequency, notice, cost or system-access exposure for us.

Silence on Vendor audit rights is better for the customer than the AUDIT preferred position, so proposing wording would introduce a right against ourselves — correctly not flagged as a deviation or a missing clause requiring a redline.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is explained by the absence of any audit clause rather than by defective drafting; it does not indicate an unaddressed risk here.

Rationale is accurate and internally consistent with the quoted text (§9 Y2K access and §8(f) technical mechanisms are correctly characterized as narrow, self-funded Vendor rights rather than usage audits).
